title: इन्टरनेटको मूल्यवृद्धिमा ‘कार्टेलिङ’ को आशंका, नियामक निकायमाथि प्रश्न
content:
No ads found for this position इन्टरनेट सेवा प्रदायकले इन्टरनेटको मूल्य वृद्धि गर्ने घोषणा गरेपछि उपभोक्तामाथि आर्थिक भार थपिने भएको छ, जसको कारण टीएससी कर दायित्वलाई देखाइएको छ। मूल्यवृद्धि कानुनी प्रक्रियाविपरीत भएको र नियामक निकायको भूमिकामा प्रश्न उठेको छ, जसले उपभोक्तालाई प्रत्यक्ष असर पारेको छ। हालका केही प्रदायकले मासिक बिलमा ५०% मर्मतसम्भार शुल्क छुट्याएर टीएससीको गणना घटाएको र यस विषयमा ठूला करदाता कार्यालयले प्रश्न उठाएको छ। After the Internet service provider announced an increase in internet prices, the financial burden on consumers will increase, due to which TSC tax liability has been pointed out. The price hike is against the legal process and has raised questions about the role of regulatory bodies, which has directly affected consumers. Some current providers have reduced the calculation of TSC by deducting a 50% maintenance fee from the monthly bill, and this has been questioned by the Large Taxpayers Office. काठमाडौं । इन्टरनेट सेवा प्रदायक (आईएसपी) हरूले इन्टरनेटको मूल्य बढाउने घोषणा गरेपछि उपभोक्तामाथि थप आर्थिक भार पर्ने भएको छ । दूरसञ्चार सेवा दस्तुर टेलिकम्युनिकेसन सर्भिस चार्ज (टीएससी) सम्बन्धी कर दायित्वलाई कारण देखाउँदै मूल्य बढाइएको भनिए पनि त्यसको अनुपात, कानुनी आधार र नियामक निकायको भूमिकामाथि गम्भीर प्रश्न उठेका छन् । इन्टरनेट सेवा प्रदायकहरूको संस्था इन्टरनेट सेवा प्रदायक संघ नेपाल (आईस्पान) को अगुवाइमा मूल्यवृद्धिमा कार्टेलिङ भएको आरोप छ । केही प्रदायकले उपभोक्ताले यसअघि तिर्दै आएको शुल्कको तुलनामा दोब्बरसम्म मूल्य बढाउन सक्ने गरी नयाँ दर घोषणा गरेका छन् । तर, इन्टरनेटको मूल्यवृद्धि गर्नुअघि कानुनअनुसार नेपाल दूरसञ्चार प्राधिकरणबाट स्वीकृति लिइएको छैन । यस प्रकरणमा नियामक नेपाल दूरसञ्चार प्राधिकरण र सञ्चार तथा सूचना प्रविधि मन्त्रालयको भूमिका पनि प्रश्नको घेरामा परेको छ । उपभोक्तालाई प्रत्यक्ष असर पर्ने गरी मूल्य बढाइएको अवस्थामा नियामक निकायले के कदम चाल्यो भन्ने प्रश्न उठेको छ। नेपाल प्रेस ले दूरसञ्चार सेवाको मूल्य निर्धारणसम्बन्धी कानुनी व्यवस्था, टीएससी विवाद र प्रमुख इन्टरनेट सेवा प्रदायकहरूको विगत सात आर्थिक वर्षको नाफासम्बन्धी विवरणलाई आधार बनाएर यस विषयको अध्ययन गरेको छ । सात वर्षको नाफा : घाटामा होइन, मुनाफामा चलेका प्रदायक नेपाल प्रेसलाई उपलब्ध गराइएको आर्थिक वर्ष २०७५/७६ देखि २०८१/८२ सम्मका केही प्रमुख इन्टरनेट सेवा प्रदायकका वार्षिक लेखापरीक्षण विवरणमा कम्पनीहरू नाफामा सञ्चालन भएको देखिन्छ । यसरी मुनाफा कमाउँदै सञ्चालनमा आउँदा समेत TSC को लागि प्रति महिना प्रति ग्राहक अधिकतमा १६ (सोह्र) रूपैयाँदेखि २५ (पच्चिस) रूपैयाँसम्म लागत बढ्ने अवस्थामा एकै पटक प्रति ग्राहक प्रति महिना १००० (एक हजार) रूपैयाँ सम्म थप बढी रकम असुल गर्न खोजिएको देखिन्छ । नियामक निकाय प्राधिकरण र सञ्चार मन्त्रालय निरीह भएका हुन् वा तिनै निकायहरूसँगको सेटिङ्गमा ISP हरुले अचाक्ली मूल्यवृद्धि गरेका हुन् ? भन्ने प्रश्न समेत उठेको छ । मूल्य निर्धारणको अधिकार प्राधिकरणलाई दूरसञ्चार ऐन, २०५३ को दफा ४२ ले दूरसञ्चार सेवाको शुल्क निर्धारणसम्बन्धी व्यवस्था अनुसार सेवाको शुल्क उचित र मनासिब हुनुपर्ने तथा शुल्क लागू गर्नुअघि कम्तीमा तीन महिनाअगावै प्राधिकरणबाट स्वीकृति लिएर सार्वजनिक गर्नुपर्ने व्यवस्था छ। सेवाको शुल्क निर्धारण गर्दा सेवा प्रदायकको वास्तविक लागतलाई आधार बनाउनुपर्ने विषय पनि महत्त्वपूर्ण हुन्छ। त्यसैले इन्टरनेट सेवा प्रदायकले मूल्य बढाउँदा लागतमा भएको वास्तविक परिवर्तन, कर दायित्व र सेवाको गुणस्तरमा आएको परिवर्तनजस्ता पक्ष स्पष्ट पार्नुपर्ने हुन्छ । यदि प्राधिकरणको स्वीकृतिबिना वा कानुनी प्रक्रियाविपरीत मूल्य बढाइएको हो भने त्यो नियामकीय परीक्षणको विषय बन्नेछ । त्यसैगरी, लागतको तुलनामा अस्वाभाविक रूपमा उच्च शुल्क निर्धारण गरिएको हो भने प्राधिकरणको दायित्व हुन्छ यसमा लगाम लगाउने । यद्यपि,मूल्यवृद्धि कानुनविपरीत भएको निष्कर्षमा पुग्नुअघि सम्बन्धित प्रदायकले सार्वजनिक गरेका दर, प्राधिकरणको स्वीकृति र लागू भएका निर्णयको आधिकारिक विवरण परीक्षण गर्न आवश्यक छ। टीएससी विवादको भार उपभोक्तामाथि ? नेपाल सरकारले आर्थिक ऐन, २०७५ देखि दूरसञ्चार सेवामा टीएससी लगाउँदै आएको छ ।सुरुमा १३ प्रतिशत रहेको यस्तो दस्तुर हाल १० प्रतिशत छ । फिक्स्ड वायर्ड ब्रोडब्यान्ड सेवामा लाग्ने महसुलको बढीमा ५० प्रतिशतसम्मको मर्मतसम्भार शुल्कमा टीएससी नलाग्ने व्यवस्था आर्थिक ऐनहरूमा गरिएका छ। तर, इन्टरनेट सेवा प्रदायकहरूले ग्राहकको मासिक बिलमा इन्टरनेट सेवा र मर्मतसम्भार सेवाको शुल्क ५०-५० प्रतिशतका दरले छुट्याएर बिलिङ गर्दै आएको विषय विवादमा छ । दूरसञ्चार नियमावली, २०५४ को नियम १५ (ज) ले सेवा बिग्रिएमा प्रदायकले निःशुल्क मर्मत गर्नुपर्ने व्यवस्था गरेको छ। २०७६ साउन १५ मा गरिएको नवौँ संशोधनबाट फिक्स्ड वायर्ड ब्रोडब्यान्ड सेवाको महसुलमा बढीमा ५० प्रतिशतसम्म मर्मतसम्भार शुल्क लिन सकिने व्यवस्था थपिएको थियो । तर, मर्मतसम्भार शुल्क लिन पाउने व्यवस्था र नियमित मासिक बिलमा स्वतः आधा रकम मर्मतसम्भारका नाममा छुट्याउन पाउने विषय एउटै होइनन्। त्यसैले बिलिङको अभ्यास नियमावली र आर्थिक ऐनको मर्मअनुकूल छ कि छैन भन्ने विषयमा स्पष्ट नियामकीय व्याख्या आवश्यक देखिन्छ। नेपाल टेलिकमबाहेकका केही इन्टरनेट सेवा प्रदायकले मासिक बिलमा इन्टरनेट र मर्मतसम्भार शुल्क बराबर देखाएर सरकारले प्राप्त गर्नुपर्ने टीएससीको गणना हुने आधार घटाएको विषयमा ठूला करदाता कार्यालयले प्रश्न उठाएको थियो। कार्यालयले आर्थिक वर्ष २०७५/७६ देखिको टीएससी र त्यसमा लाग्ने जरिवानासमेत भुक्तानी गर्न प्रदायकहरूलाई पत्राचार गरेको थियो । के छ कानुनी व्यवस्था ? दूरसञ्चार सेवा दस्तुर (Telecommunication Service Charge: TSC) को भार उपभोक्तामाथि ! नेपाल सरकारले आर्थिक ऐन, २०७५ देखि हरेक वर्ष आर्थिक ऐनहरूबाट दूरसञ्चार सेवा शुल्कमा दूरसञ्चार सेवा दस्तुर (TSC) लगाउँदै आएको छ। सुरुमा यो दस्तुर १३% थियो भने हाल आएर १०% रहेको छ। आर्थिक ऐनहरूले फिक्स्ड ब्रोडब्यान्ड सेवाको ५० प्रतिशतसम्मको मर्मत सम्भार शुल्कमा भने TSC नलाग्ने कानुनी व्यवस्था गरेका थिए। आर्थिक ऐनहरू, दूरसञ्चार ऐन, २०५३ तथा दूरसञ्चार नियमावली, २०५४ मा गरिएको व्यवस्थाअनुरूप: (१) ग्राहकको दूरसञ्चार सेवा कुनै कारणले बिग्रेमा दूरसञ्चार सेवा प्रदायकले निःशुल्क रूपमा मर्मत गरिदिनुपर्ने कानुनी व्यवस्था गरिएको – दूरसञ्चार नियमावली, २०५४ को नियम १५(ज)। (२) तर, दूरसञ्चार सेवा अन्तर्गतको फिक्स्ड वायर्ड ब्रोडब्यान्ड सेवा प्रदान गरेबापत लाग्ने महसुलमा बढीमा पचास प्रतिशतसम्म मर्मत सम्भार शुल्क लगाउन सक्ने – दूरसञ्चार नियमावली, २०५४ को नियम १५(ज) मा मिति २०७६/०४/१५ मा गरिएको नवौँ संशोधनबाट थप गरिएको प्रतिबन्धात्मक वाक्यांश। (३) दूरसञ्चार सेवा अन्तर्गतको फिक्स्ड वायर्ड ब्रोडब्यान्ड सेवा (उदाहरणका लागि FTTH Internet Service) बिग्रेको खण्डमा मर्मत गर्दा जतिसुकै खर्च लागे पनि ISPहरूले मासिक महसुलको अधिकतम ५०% सम्म मर्मत सम्भार शुल्क लिन पाउने – यो व्यवस्थाबमोजिम FTTH Internet Service बिग्रेको अवस्थामा मात्र मर्मत सम्भार शुल्क लिन पाउने हो। (४) आर्थिक ऐनहरूले दूरसञ्चार सेवा अन्तर्गतको फिक्स्ड वायर्ड ब्रोडब्यान्ड सेवा प्रदान गरेबापत लाग्ने महसुलको बढीमा पचास प्रतिशतसम्म मर्मत सम्भार शुल्कमा TSC नलाग्ने व्यवस्था गरेका छन्। (५) तर ISPहरूले मासिक बिलमै ५० : ५० गरी इन्टरनेट सेवा र मर्मत सम्भार सेवा भनी बिलिङ गरेर नेपाल सरकारले प्राप्त गर्नुपर्ने TSC को आधार नै घटाइदिएका छन्। (६) प्रकरण (५) [ङ] मा उल्लेख गरेझैँ नेपाल टेलिकमबाहेकका ISP हरूले FTTH Internet Service को मासिक बिलमा ५० : ५० गरी इन्टरनेट सेवा र मर्मत सम्भार सेवा भनी बिलिङ गरेर नेपाल सरकारले प्राप्त गर्नुपर्ने TSC को आधार नै घटाइदिएको विषयमा ठूला करदाता कार्यालयले ISP हरूलाई वि.सं. २०७५ सालदेखिका आर्थिक ऐनहरू बमोजिम हुन आउने TSC र TSC को जरिवाना (Penalty) समेत भुक्तानीका लागि पत्राचार गरेको। (७) ISPहरूले ठूला करदाता कार्यालयले आर्थिक वर्ष २०७५/७६ देखि निर्धारण गरेको TSC र TSC को Penalty रकम नबुझाउने भन्दै सर्वोच्च अदालतमा रिट दायर गरेको विषयमा पटकपटकको सुनुवाइपश्चात् सम्मानित सर्वोच्च अदालतले ISPहरूको रिट नै खारेज गरिदिएपछि ISPहरूले नेपाल सरकारलाई TSC को Penalty बाहेक पनि १२ अर्बभन्दा बढी रकम बुझाउनुपर्ने अवस्था सिर्जना भएको। (८) प्रकरण (७) [छ] मा उल्लेख गरिएअनुसार TSC रकम नेपाल सरकारलाई बुझाउनुपर्ने भएपश्चात् विगत सात वर्षभन्दा बढी समयावधिको TSC र TSC को Penalty रकम निरीह उपभोक्ताहरूमाथि लाद्नका निम्ति ISPहरूले नेपाल दूरसञ्चार प्राधिकरण र Internet service providers (ISPs) have announced an increase in internet prices, putting an additional financial burden on consumers. Although the price increase is said to be due to the tax liability related to the Telecommunication Service Charge (TSC), serious questions have been raised about its proportion, legal basis and the role of the regulatory body. There are allegations of price gouging led by the Internet Service Providers Association of Nepal (ISPAN), an organization of internet service providers. Some providers have announced new rates that could increase prices by up to double what consumers were previously paying. However, prior to increasing the price of internet, approval from the Nepal Telecommunication Authority (NTA) was not obtained as per the law. The role of the regulator, the Nepal Telecommunication Authority (NTA) and the Ministry of Communications and Information Technology (MCIT) has also been called into question in this matter. The question has been raised as to what steps the regulatory body took when prices were increased in a way that directly affected consumers. Nepal Press has studied this issue based on the legal provisions related to the pricing of telecommunication services, the TSC controversy, and the profit details of major internet service providers for the past seven fiscal years. The authority has the right to determine prices. Section 42 of the Telecommunications Act, 2053 BS, stipulates that the service fee must be fair and reasonable, and must be approved by the authority and made public at least three months before the fee is implemented. It is also important to base the service provider's actual costs on the price of the service. Therefore, when increasing the price, the Internet service provider must clarify the actual change in costs, tax liability, and changes in the quality of service. If the price is increased without the authority's approval or in violation of legal procedures, it will be subject to regulatory scrutiny. Similarly, if the fee is set abnormally high compared to the cost, the authority has the responsibility to rein it in. However, before concluding that the price increase is against the law, it is necessary to examine the rates published by the relevant provider, the authority's approval, and the official details of the decisions that have been implemented. Is the burden of the TSC controversy on consumers? The Government of Nepal has been imposing TSC on telecommunications services since the Finance Act, 2075 BS. Initially, this fee was 13 percent, but is currently 10 percent. The financial laws have made provisions to exempt maintenance charges up to a maximum of 50 percent of the fixed wired broadband service charges from TSC. However, the issue of internet service providers billing customers separately for internet service and maintenance services at a rate of 50-50 percent in their monthly bills is a matter of controversy. Rule 15(h) of the Telecommunications Regulations, 2054 BS, stipulates that the provider must repair the service free of charge if it breaks down. The ninth amendment made on 15th July 2076 BS added a provision that a maintenance fee of up to 50 percent could be charged on the fixed wired broadband service tariff. However, the provision for charging maintenance fees and the automatic allocation of half the amount in the regular monthly bill for maintenance are not the same thing. Therefore, a clear regulatory explanation is needed on whether the billing practice is in line with the spirit of the Regulations and the Finance Act. The Large Taxpayers' Office had raised questions about some internet service providers, other than Nepal Telecom, reducing the basis for calculating the TSC that the government should receive by showing the internet and maintenance fees in the monthly bill. The burden of Telecommunication Service Charge (TSC) falls on the consumer! The Government of Nepal has been imposing a Telecommunication Service Charge (TSC) on telecommunications service charges every year since the Financial Act, 2075 BS. Initially, this charge was 13%, but has now been reduced to 10%. The Financial Acts had made a legal provision that maintenance charges of up to 50 percent of fixed broadband services would not be subject to TSC. As per the provisions made in the Financial Acts, Telecommunications Act, 2053 BS and Telecommunications Regulations, 2054 BS: (1) There is a legal provision that if a customer's telecommunications service is damaged for any reason, the telecommunications service provider must repair it free of charge - Rule 15(h) of the Telecommunications Regulations, 2054. (2) However, a maximum maintenance fee of fifty percent may be imposed on the tariff charged for providing fixed wired broadband service under telecommunications services – a restrictive clause added by the ninth amendment made on 2076/04/15 to Rule 15(h) of the Telecommunications Regulations, 2054. (3) In the event of a breakdown of a fixed wired broadband service (for example, FTTH Internet Service) under telecommunications services, ISPs may charge a maintenance fee of up to a maximum of 50% of the monthly fee, regardless of the cost of repair – under this provision, maintenance fees may be charged only in the event of a breakdown of the FTTH Internet Service. (4) The Economic Acts have provided that TSC shall not be levied on maintenance charges up to a maximum of fifty percent of the charges levied for providing fixed wired broadband services under telecommunications services. (5) However, ISPs have reduced the basis of TSC that the Government of Nepal should receive by billing 50:50 for internet service and maintenance services in the monthly bill. (6) As mentioned in Case (5) [e], ISPs other than Nepal Telecom have reduced the basis of TSC to be received by the Government of Nepal by billing 50:50 as Internet service and maintenance service in the monthly bill of FTTH Internet Service, and the Large Taxpayers Office has written to the ISPs for payment of TSC and TSC penalty as per the Financial Acts of BS 2075 BS. (7) After repeated hearings on the issue of ISPs filing a writ petition in the Supreme Court alleging that they would not pay the TSC and TSC penalty amount determined by the Large Taxpayers Office since the fiscal year 2075/76, the Honorable Supreme Court dismissed the ISPs' writ petition, creating a situation where ISPs had to pay more than 12 billion rupees to the Government of Nepal in addition to the TSC penalty. (8) As mentioned in paragraph (7) [g], after the TSC amount was due to be paid to the Government of Nepal, ISPs, in collusion with the Nepal Telecommunications Authority and the Ministry of Information and Communications, have unfairly increased internet charges by up to two times in order to impose the TSC and TSC penalty amount for the past seven years on innocent consumers. (9) When comparing the billing of other ISPs with the TSC amount currently being collected and paid by Nepal Telecom from FTTH Internet customers, it appears that ISPs are increasing the cost per customer by 16 (sixteen) to 25 (twenty-five) rupees per month; however, ISPs are openly trying to loot in broad daylight by cartelizing and collecting an additional amount of up to 1000 (one thousand) rupees per month from each customer. Claims of liability exceeding Rs. 12 billion Internet service providers had filed a writ petition in the Supreme Court in a dispute over TSC determination. After the Supreme Court dismissed the writ petition of the providers, they have been forced to pay more than Rs 12 billion in TSC to the government, in addition to fines. If there is a situation where tax liabilities from previous years have to be paid, the question naturally arises as to whether the burden can be shifted to the consumer. Although the legal liability for taxes and fees lies with the service provider, it can still have an impact on pricing. However, the decision as to whether it is appropriate to increase prices all at once based on past liabilities should be based on actual costs, legal provisions, and regulatory approvals. Cost per customer is 16 to 25 rupees, price increase is up to a thousand? When comparing Nepal Telecom's FTTH internet service billing with that of other service providers, TSC will incur an additional cost of around Rs 16 to 25 per month per subscriber. In comparison, there are allegations that some providers are trying to charge an additional fee of up to Rs 1,000 per month per customer. If confirmed by the published price list and customer bills, serious questions arise about the difference between additional costs and price increases. If the price increase is many times greater than the actual additional cost incurred due to TSC, providers should disclose the basis for it. The practice of citing tax liability as the reason for the price increase but not providing a transparent breakdown of the cost undermines consumer trust. Seven years of profitability: Providers that operate in profit, not loss The annual audited accounts of some major internet service providers for the fiscal years 2075/76 to 2081/82, provided to Nepal Press, show that the companies were operating profitably. Even while operating profitably, TSC is attempting to charge an additional amount of up to 1,000 (one thousand) rupees per month per customer at a time, while the cost per customer per month for the service increases from a maximum of 16 (sixteen) rupees to 25 (twenty-five) rupees. The question has also been raised as to whether the regulatory body, the Authority and the Ministry of Communications, were innocent or whether ISPs had excessively increased prices in the settings with those same bodies.

Internet service providers (ISPs) have announced an increase in internet prices, putting an additional financial burden on consumers. Although the price increase is said to be due to the tax liability related to the Telecommunication Service Charge (TSC), serious questions have been raised about its proportion, legal basis and the role of the regulatory body. There are allegations of price gouging led by the Internet Service Providers Association of Nepal (ISPAN), an organization of internet service providers. Some providers have announced new rates that could increase prices by up to double what consumers were previously paying. However, prior to increasing the price of internet, approval from the Nepal Telecommunication Authority (NTA) was not obtained as per the law. The role of the regulator, the Nepal Telecommunication Authority (NTA) and the Ministry of Communications and Information Technology (MCIT) has also been called into question in this matter. The question has been raised as to what steps the regulatory body took when prices were increased in a way that directly affected consumers. Nepal Press has studied this issue based on the legal provisions related to the pricing of telecommunication services, the TSC controversy, and the profit details of major internet service providers for the past seven fiscal years. The authority has the right to determine prices. Section 42 of the Telecommunications Act, 2053 BS, stipulates that the service fee must be fair and reasonable, and must be approved by the authority and made public at least three months before the fee is implemented. It is also important to base the service provider's actual costs on the price of the service. Therefore, when increasing the price, the Internet service provider must clarify the actual change in costs, tax liability, and changes in the quality of service. If the price is increased without the authority's approval or in violation of legal procedures, it will be subject to regulatory scrutiny. Similarly, if the fee is set abnormally high compared to the cost, the authority has the responsibility to rein it in. However, before concluding that the price increase is against the law, it is necessary to examine the rates published by the relevant provider, the authority's approval, and the official details of the decisions that have been implemented. Is the burden of the TSC controversy on consumers? The Government of Nepal has been imposing TSC on telecommunications services since the Finance Act, 2075 BS. Initially, this fee was 13 percent, but is currently 10 percent. The financial laws have made provisions to exempt maintenance charges up to a maximum of 50 percent of the fixed wired broadband service charges from TSC. However, the issue of internet service providers billing customers separately for internet service and maintenance services at a rate of 50-50 percent in their monthly bills is a matter of controversy. Rule 15(h) of the Telecommunications Regulations, 2054 BS, stipulates that the provider must repair the service free of charge if it breaks down. The ninth amendment made on 15th July 2076 BS added a provision that a maintenance fee of up to 50 percent could be charged on the fixed wired broadband service tariff. However, the provision for charging maintenance fees and the automatic allocation of half the amount in the regular monthly bill for maintenance are not the same thing. Therefore, a clear regulatory explanation is needed on whether the billing practice is in line with the spirit of the Regulations and the Finance Act. The Large Taxpayers' Office had raised questions about some internet service providers, other than Nepal Telecom, reducing the basis for calculating the TSC that the government should receive by showing the internet and maintenance fees in the monthly bill. The office had written to the providers to pay the TSC and the fines imposed on it from the fiscal year 2075/76 onwards. What is the legal system? The burden of Telecommunication Service Charge (TSC) falls on the consumer! The Government of Nepal has been imposing a Telecommunication Service Charge (TSC) on telecommunications service charges every year since the Financial Act, 2075 BS. Initially, this charge was 13%, but has now been reduced to 10%. The Financial Acts had made a legal provision that maintenance charges of up to 50 percent of fixed broadband services would not be subject to TSC. As per the provisions made in the Financial Acts, Telecommunications Act, 2053 BS and Telecommunications Regulations, 2054 BS: (1) There is a legal provision that if a customer's telecommunications service is damaged for any reason, the telecommunications service provider must repair it free of charge - Rule 15(h) of the Telecommunications Regulations, 2054. (2) However, a maximum maintenance fee of fifty percent may be imposed on the tariff charged for providing fixed wired broadband service under telecommunications services – a restrictive clause added by the ninth amendment made on 2076/04/15 to Rule 15(h) of the Telecommunications Regulations, 2054. (3) In the event of a breakdown of a fixed wired broadband service (for example, FTTH Internet Service) under telecommunications services, ISPs may charge a maintenance fee of up to a maximum of 50% of the monthly fee, regardless of the cost of repair – under this provision, maintenance fees may be charged only in the event of a breakdown of the FTTH Internet Service. (4) The Economic Acts have provided that TSC shall not be levied on maintenance charges up to a maximum of fifty percent of the charges levied for providing fixed wired broadband services under telecommunications services. (5) However, ISPs have reduced the basis of TSC that the Government of Nepal should receive by billing 50:50 for internet service and maintenance services in the monthly bill. (6) As mentioned in Case (5) [e], ISPs other than Nepal Telecom have reduced the basis of TSC to be received by the Government of Nepal by billing 50:50 as Internet service and maintenance service in the monthly bill of FTTH Internet Service, and the Large Taxpayers Office has written to the ISPs for payment of TSC and TSC penalty as per the Financial Acts of BS 2075 BS. (7) After repeated hearings on the issue of ISPs filing a writ petition in the Supreme Court alleging that they would not pay the TSC and TSC penalty amount determined by the Large Taxpayers Office since the fiscal year 2075/76, the Honorable Supreme Court dismissed the ISPs' writ petition, creating a situation where ISPs had to pay more than 12 billion rupees to the Government of Nepal in addition to the TSC penalty. (8) As mentioned in paragraph (7) [g], after the TSC amount was due to be paid to the Government of Nepal, ISPs, in collusion with the Nepal Telecommunications Authority and the Ministry of Information and Communications, have unfairly increased internet charges by up to two times in order to impose the TSC and TSC penalty amount for the past seven years on innocent consumers. (9) When comparing the billing of other ISPs with the TSC amount currently being collected and paid by Nepal Telecom from FTTH Internet customers, it appears that ISPs are increasing the cost per customer by 16 (sixteen) to 25 (twenty-five) rupees per month; however, ISPs are openly trying to loot in broad daylight by cartelizing and collecting an additional amount of up to 1000 (one thousand) rupees per month from each customer. Claims of liability exceeding Rs. 12 billion Internet service providers had filed a writ petition in the Supreme Court in a dispute over TSC determination. After the Supreme Court dismissed the writ petition of the providers, they have been forced to pay more than Rs 12 billion in TSC to the government, in addition to fines. If there is a situation where tax liabilities from previous years have to be paid, the question naturally arises as to whether the burden can be shifted to the consumer. Although the legal liability for taxes and fees lies with the service provider, it can still have an impact on pricing. However, the decision as to whether it is appropriate to increase prices all at once based on past liabilities should be based on actual costs, legal provisions, and regulatory approvals. Cost per customer is 16 to 25 rupees, price increase is up to a thousand? When comparing Nepal Telecom's FTTH internet service billing with that of other service providers, TSC will incur an additional cost of around Rs 16 to 25 per month per subscriber. In comparison, there are allegations that some providers are trying to charge an additional fee of up to Rs 1,000 per month per customer. If confirmed by the published price list and customer bills, serious questions arise about the difference between additional costs and price increases. If the price increase is many times greater than the actual additional cost incurred due to TSC, providers should disclose the basis for it. The practice of citing tax liability as the reason for the price increase but not providing a transparent breakdown of the cost undermines consumer trust. Seven years of profitability: Providers that operate in profit, not loss The annual audited accounts of some major internet service providers for the fiscal years 2075/76 to 2081/82, provided to Nepal Press, show that the companies were operating profitably. Internet service providers (ISPs) have announced an increase in internet prices, putting an additional financial burden on consumers. Although the price increase is said to be due to the tax liability related to the Telecommunication Service Charge (TSC), serious questions have been raised about its proportion, legal basis and the role of the regulatory body. There are allegations of price gouging led by the Internet Service Providers Association of Nepal (ISPAN), an organization of internet service providers. Some providers have announced new rates that could increase prices by up to double what consumers were previously paying. However, prior to increasing the price of internet, approval from the Nepal Telecommunication Authority (NTA) was not obtained as per the law. The role of the regulator, the Nepal Telecommunication Authority (NTA) and the Ministry of Communications and Information Technology (MCIT) has also been called into question in this matter. The question has been raised as to what steps the regulatory body took when prices were increased in a way that directly affected consumers. Nepal Press has studied this issue based on the legal provisions related to the pricing of telecommunication services, the TSC controversy, and the profit details of major internet service providers for the past seven fiscal years. The authority has the right to determine prices. Section 42 of the Telecommunications Act, 2053 BS, stipulates that the service fee must be fair and reasonable, and must be approved by the authority and made public at least three months before the fee is implemented. It is also important to base the service provider's actual costs on the price of the service. Therefore, when increasing the price, the Internet service provider must clarify the actual change in costs, tax liability, and changes in the quality of service. If the price is increased without the authority's approval or in violation of legal procedures, it will be subject to regulatory scrutiny. Similarly, if the fee is set abnormally high compared to the cost, the authority has the responsibility to rein it in. However, before concluding that the price increase is against the law, it is necessary to examine the rates published by the relevant provider, the authority's approval, and the official details of the decisions that have been implemented. Is the burden of the TSC controversy on consumers? The Government of Nepal has been imposing TSC on telecommunications services since the Finance Act, 2075 BS. Initially, this fee was 13 percent, but is currently 10 percent. The financial laws have made provisions to exempt maintenance charges up to a maximum of 50 percent of the fixed wired broadband service charges from TSC. However, the issue of internet service providers billing customers separately for internet service and maintenance services at a rate of 50-50 percent in their monthly bills is a matter of controversy. Rule 15(h) of the Telecommunications Regulations, 2054 BS, stipulates that the provider must repair the service free of charge if it breaks down. The ninth amendment made on 15th July 2076 BS added a provision that a maintenance fee of up to 50 percent could be charged on the fixed wired broadband service tariff. However, the provision for charging maintenance fees and the automatic allocation of half the amount in the regular monthly bill for maintenance are not the same thing. Therefore, a clear regulatory explanation is needed on whether the billing practice is in line with the spirit of the Regulations and the Finance Act. The Large Taxpayers' Office had raised questions about some internet service providers, other than Nepal Telecom, reducing the basis for calculating the TSC that the government should receive by showing the internet and maintenance fees in the monthly bill. The burden of Telecommunication Service Charge (TSC) falls on the consumer! The Government of Nepal has been imposing a Telecommunication Service Charge (TSC) on telecommunications service charges every year since the Financial Act, 2075 BS. Initially, this charge was 13%, but has now been reduced to 10%. The Financial Acts had made a legal provision that maintenance charges of up to 50 percent of fixed broadband services would not be subject to TSC. As per the provisions made in the Financial Acts, Telecommunications Act, 2053 BS and Telecommunications Regulations, 2054 BS: (1) There is a legal provision that if a customer's telecommunications service is damaged for any reason, the telecommunications service provider must repair it free of charge - Rule 15(h) of the Telecommunications Regulations, 2054. (2) However, a maximum maintenance fee of fifty percent may be imposed on the tariff charged for providing fixed wired broadband service under telecommunications services – a restrictive clause added by the ninth amendment made on 2076/04/15 to Rule 15(h) of the Telecommunications Regulations, 2054. (3) In the event of a breakdown of a fixed wired broadband service (for example, FTTH Internet Service) under telecommunications services, ISPs may charge a maintenance fee of up to a maximum of 50% of the monthly fee, regardless of the cost of repair – under this provision, maintenance fees may be charged only in the event of a breakdown of the FTTH Internet Service. (4) The Economic Acts have provided that TSC shall not be levied on maintenance charges up to a maximum of fifty percent of the charges levied for providing fixed wired broadband services under telecommunications services. (5) However, ISPs have reduced the basis of TSC that the Government of Nepal should receive by billing 50:50 for internet service and maintenance services in the monthly bill. (6) As mentioned in Case (5) [e], ISPs other than Nepal Telecom have reduced the basis of TSC to be received by the Government of Nepal by billing 50:50 as Internet service and maintenance service in the monthly bill of FTTH Internet Service, and the Large Taxpayers Office has written to the ISPs for payment of TSC and TSC penalty as per the Financial Acts of BS 2075 BS. (7) After repeated hearings on the issue of ISPs filing a writ petition in the Supreme Court alleging that they would not pay the TSC and TSC penalty amount determined by the Large Taxpayers Office since the fiscal year 2075/76, the Honorable Supreme Court dismissed the ISPs' writ petition, creating a situation where ISPs had to pay more than 12 billion rupees to the Government of Nepal in addition to the TSC penalty. (8) As mentioned in paragraph (7) [g], after the TSC amount was due to be paid to the Government of Nepal, ISPs, in collusion with the Nepal Telecommunications Authority and the Ministry of Information and Communications, have unfairly increased internet charges by up to two times in order to impose the TSC and TSC penalty amount for the past seven years on innocent consumers. (9) When comparing the billing of other ISPs with the TSC amount currently being collected and paid by Nepal Telecom from FTTH Internet customers, it appears that ISPs are increasing the cost per customer by 16 (sixteen) to 25 (twenty-five) rupees per month; however, ISPs are openly trying to loot in broad daylight by cartelizing and collecting an additional amount of up to 1000 (one thousand) rupees per month from each customer. Claims of liability exceeding Rs. 12 billion Internet service providers had filed a writ petition in the Supreme Court in a dispute over TSC determination. After the Supreme Court dismissed the writ petition of the providers, they have been forced to pay more than Rs 12 billion in TSC to the government, in addition to fines. If there is a situation where tax liabilities from previous years have to be paid, the question naturally arises as to whether the burden can be shifted to the consumer. Although the legal liability for taxes and fees lies with the service provider, it can still have an impact on pricing. However, the decision as to whether it is appropriate to increase prices all at once based on past liabilities should be based on actual costs, legal provisions, and regulatory approvals. Cost per customer is 16 to 25 rupees, price increase is up to a thousand? When comparing Nepal Telecom's FTTH internet service billing with that of other service providers, TSC will incur an additional cost of around Rs 16 to 25 per month per subscriber. In comparison, there are allegations that some providers are trying to charge an additional fee of up to Rs 1,000 per month per customer. If confirmed by the published price list and customer bills, serious questions arise about the difference between additional costs and price increases. If the price increase is many times greater than the actual additional cost incurred due to TSC, providers should disclose the basis for it. The practice of citing tax liability as the reason for the price increase but not providing a transparent breakdown of the cost undermines consumer trust. Seven years of profitability: Providers that operate in profit, not loss The annual audited accounts of some major internet service providers for the fiscal years 2075/76 to 2081/82, provided to Nepal Press, show that the companies were operating profitably. Even while operating profitably, TSC is attempting to charge an additional amount of up to 1,000 (one thousand) rupees per month per customer at a time, while the cost per customer per month for the service increases from a maximum of 16 (sixteen) rupees to 25 (twenty-five) rupees. The question has also been raised as to whether the regulatory body, the Authority and the Ministry of Communications, were innocent or whether ISPs had excessively increased prices in the settings with those same bodies.

Internet service providers (ISPs) have announced an increase in internet prices, putting an additional financial burden on consumers. Although the price increase is said to be due to the tax liability related to the Telecommunication Service Charge (TSC), serious questions have been raised about its proportion, legal basis and the role of the regulatory body. There are allegations of price gouging led by the Internet Service Providers Association of Nepal (ISPAN), an organization of internet service providers. Some providers have announced new rates that could increase prices by up to double what consumers were previously paying. However, prior to increasing the price of internet, approval from the Nepal Telecommunication Authority (NTA) was not obtained as per the law. The role of the regulator, the Nepal Telecommunication Authority (NTA) and the Ministry of Communications and Information Technology (MCIT) has also been called into question in this matter. The question has been raised as to what steps the regulatory body took when prices were increased in a way that directly affected consumers. Nepal Press has studied this issue based on the legal provisions related to the pricing of telecommunication services, the TSC controversy, and the profit details of major internet service providers for the past seven fiscal years. The authority has the right to determine prices. Section 42 of the Telecommunications Act, 2053 BS, stipulates that the service fee must be fair and reasonable, and must be approved by the authority and made public at least three months before the fee is implemented. It is also important to base the service provider's actual costs on the price of the service. Therefore, when increasing the price, the Internet service provider must clarify the actual change in costs, tax liability, and changes in the quality of service. If the price is increased without the authority's approval or in violation of legal procedures, it will be subject to regulatory scrutiny. Similarly, if the fee is set abnormally high compared to the cost, the authority has the responsibility to rein it in. However, before concluding that the price increase is against the law, it is necessary to examine the rates published by the relevant provider, the authority's approval, and the official details of the decisions that have been implemented. Is the burden of the TSC controversy on consumers? The Government of Nepal has been imposing TSC on telecommunications services since the Finance Act, 2075 BS. Initially, this fee was 13 percent, but is currently 10 percent. The financial laws have made provisions to exempt maintenance charges up to a maximum of 50 percent of the fixed wired broadband service charges from TSC. However, the issue of internet service providers billing customers separately for internet service and maintenance services at a rate of 50-50 percent in their monthly bills is a matter of controversy. Rule 15(h) of the Telecommunications Regulations, 2054 BS, stipulates that the provider must repair the service free of charge if it breaks down. The ninth amendment made on 15th July 2076 BS added a provision that a maintenance fee of up to 50 percent could be charged on the fixed wired broadband service tariff. However, the provision for charging maintenance fees and the automatic allocation of half the amount in the regular monthly bill for maintenance are not the same thing. Therefore, a clear regulatory explanation is needed on whether the billing practice is in line with the spirit of the Regulations and the Finance Act. The Large Taxpayers' Office had raised questions about some internet service providers, other than Nepal Telecom, reducing the basis for calculating the TSC that the government should receive by showing the internet and maintenance fees in the monthly bill. The office had written to the providers to pay the TSC and the fines imposed on it from the fiscal year 2075/76 onwards. What is the legal system? The burden of Telecommunication Service Charge (TSC) falls on the consumer! The Government of Nepal has been imposing a Telecommunication Service Charge (TSC) on telecommunications service charges every year since the Financial Act, 2075 BS. Initially, this charge was 13%, but has now been reduced to 10%. The Financial Acts had made a legal provision that maintenance charges of up to 50 percent of fixed broadband services would not be subject to TSC. As per the provisions made in the Financial Acts, Telecommunications Act, 2053 BS and Telecommunications Regulations, 2054 BS: (1) There is a legal provision that if a customer's telecommunications service is damaged for any reason, the telecommunications service provider must repair it free of charge - Rule 15(h) of the Telecommunications Regulations, 2054. (2) However, a maximum maintenance fee of fifty percent may be imposed on the tariff charged for providing fixed wired broadband service under telecommunications services – a restrictive clause added by the ninth amendment made on 2076/04/15 to Rule 15(h) of the Telecommunications Regulations, 2054. (3) In the event of a breakdown of a fixed wired broadband service (for example, FTTH Internet Service) under telecommunications services, ISPs may charge a maintenance fee of up to a maximum of 50% of the monthly fee, regardless of the cost of repair – under this provision, maintenance fees may be charged only in the event of a breakdown of the FTTH Internet Service. (4) The Economic Acts have provided that TSC shall not be levied on maintenance charges up to a maximum of fifty percent of the charges levied for providing fixed wired broadband services under telecommunications services. (5) However, ISPs have reduced the basis of TSC that the Government of Nepal should receive by billing 50:50 for internet service and maintenance services in the monthly bill. (6) As mentioned in Case (5) [e], ISPs other than Nepal Telecom have reduced the basis of TSC to be received by the Government of Nepal by billing 50:50 as Internet service and maintenance service in the monthly bill of FTTH Internet Service, and the Large Taxpayers Office has written to the ISPs for payment of TSC and TSC penalty as per the Financial Acts of BS 2075 BS. (7) After repeated hearings on the issue of ISPs filing a writ petition in the Supreme Court alleging that they would not pay the TSC and TSC penalty amount determined by the Large Taxpayers Office since the fiscal year 2075/76, the Honorable Supreme Court dismissed the ISPs' writ petition, creating a situation where ISPs had to pay more than 12 billion rupees to the Government of Nepal in addition to the TSC penalty. (8) As mentioned in paragraph (7) [g], after the TSC amount was due to be paid to the Government of Nepal, ISPs, in collusion with the Nepal Telecommunications Authority and the Ministry of Information and Communications, have unfairly increased internet charges by up to two times in order to impose the TSC and TSC penalty amount for the past seven years on innocent consumers. (9) When comparing the billing of other ISPs with the TSC amount currently being collected and paid by Nepal Telecom from FTTH Internet customers, it appears that ISPs are increasing the cost per customer by 16 (sixteen) to 25 (twenty-five) rupees per month; however, ISPs are openly trying to loot in broad daylight by cartelizing and collecting an additional amount of up to 1000 (one thousand) rupees per month from each customer. Claims of liability exceeding Rs. 12 billion Internet service providers had filed a writ petition in the Supreme Court in a dispute over TSC determination. After the Supreme Court dismissed the writ petition of the providers, they have been forced to pay more than Rs 12 billion in TSC to the government, in addition to fines. If there is a situation where tax liabilities from previous years have to be paid, the question naturally arises as to whether the burden can be shifted to the consumer. Although the legal liability for taxes and fees lies with the service provider, it can still have an impact on pricing. However, the decision as to whether it is appropriate to increase prices all at once based on past liabilities should be based on actual costs, legal provisions, and regulatory approvals. Cost per customer is 16 to 25 rupees, price increase is up to a thousand? When comparing Nepal Telecom's FTTH internet service billing with that of other service providers, TSC will incur an additional cost of around Rs 16 to 25 per month per subscriber. In comparison, there are allegations that some providers are trying to charge an additional fee of up to Rs 1,000 per month per customer. If confirmed by the published price list and customer bills, serious questions arise about the difference between additional costs and price increases. If the price increase is many times greater than the actual additional cost incurred due to TSC, providers should disclose the basis for it. The practice of citing tax liability as the reason for the price increase but not providing a transparent breakdown of the cost undermines consumer trust. Seven years of profitability: Providers that operate in profit, not loss The annual audited accounts of some major internet service providers for the fiscal years 2075/76 to 2081/82, provided to Nepal Press, show that the companies were operating profitably. Internet service providers (ISPs) have announced an increase in internet prices, putting an additional financial burden on consumers. Although the price increase is said to be due to the tax liability related to the Telecommunication Service Charge (TSC), serious questions have been raised about its proportion, legal basis and the role of the regulatory body. There are allegations of price gouging led by the Internet Service Providers Association of Nepal (ISPAN), an organization of internet service providers. Some providers have announced new rates that could increase prices by up to double what consumers were previously paying. However, prior to increasing the price of internet, approval from the Nepal Telecommunication Authority (NTA) was not obtained as per the law. The role of the regulator, the Nepal Telecommunication Authority (NTA) and the Ministry of Communications and Information Technology (MCIT) has also been called into question in this matter. The question has been raised as to what steps the regulatory body took when prices were increased in a way that directly affected consumers. Nepal Press has studied this issue based on the legal provisions related to the pricing of telecommunication services, the TSC controversy, and the profit details of major internet service providers for the past seven fiscal years. The authority has the right to determine prices. Section 42 of the Telecommunications Act, 2053 BS, stipulates that the service fee must be fair and reasonable, and must be approved by the authority and made public at least three months before the fee is implemented. It is also important to base the service provider's actual costs on the price of the service. Therefore, when increasing the price, the Internet service provider must clarify the actual change in costs, tax liability, and changes in the quality of service. If the price is increased without the authority's approval or in violation of legal procedures, it will be subject to regulatory scrutiny. Similarly, if the fee is set abnormally high compared to the cost, the authority has the responsibility to rein it in. However, before concluding that the price increase is against the law, it is necessary to examine the rates published by the relevant provider, the authority's approval, and the official details of the decisions that have been implemented. Is the burden of the TSC controversy on consumers? The Government of Nepal has been imposing TSC on telecommunications services since the Finance Act, 2075 BS. Initially, this fee was 13 percent, but is currently 10 percent. The financial laws have made provisions to exempt maintenance charges up to a maximum of 50 percent of the fixed wired broadband service charges from TSC. However, the issue of internet service providers billing customers separately for internet service and maintenance services at a rate of 50-50 percent in their monthly bills is a matter of controversy. Rule 15(h) of the Telecommunications Regulations, 2054 BS, stipulates that the provider must repair the service free of charge if it breaks down. The ninth amendment made on 15th July 2076 BS added a provision that a maintenance fee of up to 50 percent could be charged on the fixed wired broadband service tariff. However, the provision for charging maintenance fees and the automatic allocation of half the amount in the regular monthly bill for maintenance are not the same thing. Therefore, a clear regulatory explanation is needed on whether the billing practice is in line with the spirit of the Regulations and the Finance Act. The Large Taxpayers' Office had raised questions about some internet service providers, other than Nepal Telecom, reducing the basis for calculating the TSC that the government should receive by showing the internet and maintenance fees in the monthly bill. The office had written to the providers to pay the TSC and the fines imposed on it from the fiscal year 2075/76 onwards. What is the legal system? The burden of Telecommunication Service Charge (TSC) falls on the consumer! The Government of Nepal has been imposing a Telecommunication Service Charge (TSC) on telecommunications service charges every year since the Financial Act, 2075 BS. Initially, this charge was 13%, but has now been reduced to 10%. The Financial Acts had made a legal provision that maintenance charges of up to 50 percent of fixed broadband services would not be subject to TSC. As per the provisions made in the Financial Acts, Telecommunications Act, 2053 BS and Telecommunications Regulations, 2054 BS: (1) There is a legal provision that if a customer's telecommunications service is damaged for any reason, the telecommunications service provider must repair it free of charge - Rule 15(h) of the Telecommunications Regulations, 2054. (2) However, a maximum maintenance fee of fifty percent may be imposed on the tariff charged for providing fixed wired broadband service under telecommunications services – a restrictive clause added by the ninth amendment made on 2076/04/15 to Rule 15(h) of the Telecommunications Regulations, 2054. (3) In the event of a breakdown of a fixed wired broadband service (for example, FTTH Internet Service) under telecommunications services, ISPs may charge a maintenance fee of up to a maximum of 50% of the monthly fee, regardless of the cost of repair – under this provision, maintenance fees may be charged only in the event of a breakdown of the FTTH Internet Service. (4) The Economic Acts have provided that TSC shall not be levied on maintenance charges up to a maximum of fifty percent of the charges levied for providing fixed wired broadband services under telecommunications services. (5) However, ISPs have reduced the basis of TSC that the Government of Nepal should receive by billing 50:50 for internet service and maintenance services in the monthly bill. (6) As mentioned in Case (5) [e], ISPs other than Nepal Telecom have reduced the basis of TSC to be received by the Government of Nepal by billing 50:50 as Internet service and maintenance service in the monthly bill of FTTH Internet Service, and the Large Taxpayers Office has written to the ISPs for payment of TSC and TSC penalty as per the Financial Acts of BS 2075 BS. (7) After repeated hearings on the issue of ISPs filing a writ petition in the Supreme Court alleging that they would not pay the TSC and TSC penalty amount determined by the Large Taxpayers Office since the fiscal year 2075/76, the Honorable Supreme Court dismissed the ISPs' writ petition, creating a situation where ISPs had to pay more than 12 billion rupees to the Government of Nepal in addition to the TSC penalty. (8) As mentioned in paragraph (7) [g], after the TSC amount was due to be paid to the Government of Nepal, ISPs, in collusion with the Nepal Telecommunications Authority and the Ministry of Information and Communications, have unfairly increased internet charges by up to two times in order to impose the TSC and TSC penalty amount for the past seven years on innocent consumers. (9) When comparing the billing of other ISPs with the TSC amount currently being collected and paid by Nepal Telecom from FTTH Internet customers, it appears that ISPs are increasing the cost per customer by 16 (sixteen) to 25 (twenty-five) rupees per month; however, ISPs are openly trying to loot in broad daylight by cartelizing and collecting an additional amount of up to 1000 (one thousand) rupees per month from each customer. Claims of liability exceeding Rs. 12 billion Internet service providers had filed a writ petition in the Supreme Court in a dispute over TSC determination. After the Supreme Court dismissed the writ petition of the providers, they have been forced to pay more than Rs 12 billion in TSC to the government, in addition to fines. If there is a situation where tax liabilities from previous years have to be paid, the question naturally arises as to whether the burden can be shifted to the consumer. Although the legal liability for taxes and fees lies with the service provider, it can still have an impact on pricing. However, the decision as to whether it is appropriate to increase prices all at once based on past liabilities should be based on actual costs, legal provisions, and regulatory approvals. Cost per customer is 16 to 25 rupees, price increase is up to a thousand? When comparing Nepal Telecom's FTTH internet service billing with that of other service providers, TSC will incur an additional cost of around Rs 16 to 25 per month per subscriber. In comparison, there are allegations that some providers are trying to charge an additional fee of up to Rs 1,000 per month per customer. If confirmed by the published price list and customer bills, serious questions arise about the difference between additional costs and price increases. If the price increase is many times greater than the actual additional cost incurred due to TSC, providers should disclose the basis for it. The practice of citing tax liability as the reason for the price increase but not providing a transparent breakdown of the cost undermines consumer trust. Seven years of profitability: Providers that operate in profit, not loss The annual audited accounts of some major internet service providers for the fiscal years 2075/76 to 2081/82, provided to Nepal Press, show that the companies were operating profitably. Even while operating profitably, TSC is attempting to charge an additional amount of up to 1,000 (one thousand) rupees per month per customer at a time, while the cost per customer per month for the service increases from a maximum of 16 (sixteen) rupees to 25 (twenty-five) rupees. The question has also been raised as to whether the regulatory body, the Authority and the Ministry of Communications, were innocent or whether ISPs had excessively increased prices in the settings with those same bodies.

नियमावली, २०५४ को नियम १५ (ज) ले सेवा बिग्रिएमा प्रदायकले निःशुल्क मर्मत गर्नुपर्ने व्यवस्था गरेको छ। २०७६ साउन १५ मा गरिएको नवौँ संशोधनबाट फिक्स्ड वायर्ड ब्रोडब्यान्ड सेवाको महसुलमा बढीमा ५० प्रतिशतसम्म मर्मतसम्भार शुल्क लिन सकिने व्यवस्था थपिएको थियो । तर, मर्मतसम्भार शुल्क लिन पाउने व्यवस्था र नियमित मासिक बिलमा स्वतः आधा रकम मर्मतसम्भारका नाममा छुट्याउन पाउने विषय एउटै होइनन्। त्यसैले बिलिङको अभ्यास नियमावली र आर्थिक ऐनको मर्मअनुकूल छ कि छैन भन्ने विषयमा स्पष्ट नियामकीय व्याख्या आवश्यक देखिन्छ। नेपाल टेलिकमबाहेकका केही इन्टरनेट सेवा प्रदायकले मासिक बिलमा इन्टरनेट र मर्मतसम्भार शुल्क बराबर देखाएर सरकारले प्राप्त गर्नुपर्ने टीएससीको गणना हुने आधार घटाएको विषयमा ठूला करदाता कार्यालयले प्रश्न उठाएको थियो। कार्यालयले आर्थिक वर्ष २०७५/७६ देखिको टीएससी र त्यसमा लाग्ने जरिवानासमेत भुक्तानी गर्न प्रदायकहरूलाई पत्राचार गरेको थियो । के छ कानुनी व्यवस्था ? दूरसञ्चार सेवा दस्तुर (Telecommunication Service Charge: TSC) को भार उपभोक्तामाथि ! नेपाल सरकारले आर्थिक ऐन, २०७५ देखि हरेक वर्ष आर्थिक ऐनहरूबाट दूरसञ्चार सेवा शुल्कमा दूरसञ्चार सेवा दस्तुर (TSC) लगाउँदै आएको छ। सुरुमा यो दस्तुर १३% थियो भने हाल आएर १०% रहेको छ। आर्थिक ऐनहरूले फिक्स्ड ब्रोडब्यान्ड सेवाको ५० प्रतिशतसम्मको मर्मत सम्भार शुल्कमा भने TSC नलाग्ने कानुनी व्यवस्था गरेका थिए। आर्थिक ऐनहरू, दूरसञ्चार ऐन, २०५३ तथा दूरसञ्चार नियमावली, २०५४ मा गरिएको व्यवस्थाअनुरूप: (१) ग्राहकको दूरसञ्चार सेवा कुनै कारणले बिग्रेमा दूरसञ्चार सेवा प्रदायकले निःशुल्क रूपमा मर्मत गरिदिनुपर्ने कानुनी व्यवस्था गरिएको – दूरसञ्चार नियमावली, २०५४ को नियम १५(ज)। (२) तर, दूरसञ्चार सेवा अन्तर्गतको फिक्स्ड वायर्ड ब्रोडब्यान्ड सेवा प्रदान गरेबापत लाग्ने महसुलमा बढीमा पचास प्रतिशतसम्म मर्मत सम्भार शुल्क लगाउन सक्ने – दूरसञ्चार नियमावली, २०५४ को नियम १५(ज) मा मिति २०७६/०४/१५ मा गरिएको नवौँ संशोधनबाट थप गरिएको प्रतिबन्धात्मक वाक्यांश। (३) दूरसञ्चार सेवा अन्तर्गतको फिक्स्ड वायर्ड ब्रोडब्यान्ड सेवा (उदाहरणका लागि FTTH Internet Service) बिग्रेको खण्डमा मर्मत गर्दा जतिसुकै खर्च लागे पनि ISPहरूले मासिक महसुलको अधिकतम ५०% सम्म मर्मत सम्भार शुल्क लिन पाउने – यो व्यवस्थाबमोजिम FTTH Internet Service बिग्रेको अवस्थामा मात्र मर्मत सम्भार शुल्क लिन पाउने हो। (४) आर्थिक ऐनहरूले दूरसञ्चार सेवा अन्तर्गतको फिक्स्ड वायर्ड ब्रोडब्यान्ड सेवा प्रदान गरेबापत लाग्ने महसुलको बढीमा पचास प्रतिशतसम्म मर्मत सम्भार शुल्कमा TSC नलाग्ने व्यवस्था गरेका छन्। (५) तर ISPहरूले मासिक बिलमै ५० : ५० गरी इन्टरनेट सेवा र मर्मत सम्भार सेवा भनी बिलिङ गरेर नेपाल सरकारले प्राप्त गर्नुपर्ने TSC को आधार नै घटाइदिएका छन्। (६) प्रकरण (५) [ङ] मा उल्लेख गरेझैँ नेपाल टेलिकमबाहेकका ISP हरूले FTTH Internet Service को मासिक बिलमा ५० : ५० गरी इन्टरनेट सेवा र मर्मत सम्भार सेवा भनी बिलिङ गरेर नेपाल सरकारले प्राप्त गर्नुपर्ने TSC को आधार नै घटाइदिएको विषयमा ठूला करदाता कार्यालयले ISP हरूलाई वि.सं. २०७५ सालदेखिका आर्थिक ऐनहरू बमोजिम हुन आउने TSC र TSC को जरिवाना (Penalty) समेत भुक्तानीका लागि पत्राचार गरेको। (७) ISPहरूले ठूला करदाता कार्यालयले आर्थिक वर्ष २०७५/७६ देखि निर्धारण गरेको TSC र TSC को Penalty रकम नबुझाउने भन्दै सर्वोच्च अदालतमा रिट दायर गरेको विषयमा पटकपटकको सुनुवाइपश्चात् सम्मानित सर्वोच्च अदालतले ISPहरूको रिट नै खारेज गरिदिएपछि ISPहरूले नेपाल सरकारलाई TSC को Penalty बाहेक पनि १२ अर्बभन्दा बढी रकम बुझाउनुपर्ने अवस्था सिर्जना भएको। (८) प्रकरण (७) [छ] मा उल्लेख गरिएअनुसार TSC रकम नेपाल सरकारलाई बुझाउनुपर्ने भएपश्चात् विगत सात वर्षभन्दा बढी समयावधिको TSC र TSC को Penalty रकम निरीह उपभोक्ताहरूमाथि लाद्नका निम्ति ISPहरूले नेपाल दूरसञ्चार प्राधिकरण र सूचना तथा सञ्चार मन्त्रालयसँगको मिलेमतोमा अन्यायपूर्ण ढङ्गबाट इन्टरनेटको शुल्क दोब्बरसम्म वृद्धि गरेको। (९) हाल नेपाल टेलिकमले FTTH Internet का ग्राहकहरूबाट उठाई बुझाइरहेको TSC रकमसँग अन्य ISPहरूको बिलिङ तुलना गर्दा ISP हरूले एउटा ग्राहकबापत प्रतिमहिना १६ (सोह्र) रुपैयाँदेखि २५ (पच्चीस) रुपैयाँसम्म लागत बढ्ने देखिन्छ; तर, ISP हरूले कार्टेलिङ गरी प्रत्येक ग्राहकबाट प्रतिमहिना १००० (एक हजार) रुपैयाँसम्म थप रकम असुलउपर गरी दिनदहाडै खुलेआम रूपमा लुट मच्चाउन खोजेको देखिन्छ। १२ अर्बभन्दा बढी दायित्वको दाबी टीएससी निर्धारणसम्बन्धी विवादमा इन्टरनेट सेवा प्रदायकहरूले सर्वोच्च अदालतमा रिट दायर गरेका थिए।सर्वोच्च अदालतले प्रदायकहरूको रिट खारेज गरेपछि उनीहरूले सरकारलाई जरिवानाबाहेक १२ अर्ब रुपैयाँभन्दा बढी टीएससी बुझाउनुपर्ने अवस्था सिर्जना भएको छ । विगतका वर्षको कर दायित्व भुक्तानी गर्नुपर्ने अवस्था बनेको हो भने त्यसको भार उपभोक्तामाथि सार्न मिल्छ कि मिल्दैन भन्ने प्रश्न स्वाभाविक रूपमा उठ्छ। कर तथा दस्तुरसम्बन्धी कानुनी दायित्व सेवा प्रदायकको भए पनि मूल्य निर्धारणमा त्यसको प्रभाव पर्न सक्छ। तर, विगतको दायित्वलाई आधार बनाएर एकैपटक अत्यधिक मूल्य बढाउनु उचित हुन्छ कि हुँदैन भन्ने निर्णय वास्तविक लागत, कानुनी व्यवस्था र नियामकीय स्वीकृतिका आधारमा हुनुपर्छ। प्रतिग्राहक १६ देखि २५ रुपैयाँ लागत, मूल्यवृद्धि भने हजारसम्म ? नेपाल टेलिकमको एफटीटीएच इन्टरनेट सेवाको बिलिङसँग अन्य सेवा प्रदायकको बिलिङ तुलना गर्दा टीएससीका कारण प्रतिग्राहक प्रतिमहिना करिब १६ देखि २५ रुपैयाँसम्म अतिरिक्त लागत पर्नेछ । त्यसको तुलनामा केही प्रदायकले प्रतिग्राहक प्रतिमहिना एक हजार रुपैयाँसम्म थप शुल्क असुल्न खोजेको आरोप समेत छ । सार्वजनिक गरिएको मूल्यसूची र ग्राहकको बिलबाट पुष्टि हुन्छ भने अतिरिक्त लागत र मूल्यवृद्धिबीचको अन्तरबारे गम्भीर प्रश्न उठ्छ। टीएससीका कारण परेको वास्तविक अतिरिक्त लागतभन्दा धेरै गुणा बढी मूल्य बढाइएको हो भने प्रदायकहरूले त्यसको आधार सार्वजनिक गर्नुपर्ने हुन्छ। कर दायित्वलाई मूल्यवृद्धिको कारण देखाउने तर लागतको पारदर्शी विवरण नदिने अभ्यासले उपभोक्ताको विश्वास कमजोर बनाउँछ।

काठमाडौं । इन्टरनेट सेवा प्रदायक (आईएसपी) हरूले इन्टरनेटको मूल्य बढाउने घोषणा गरेपछि उपभोक्तामाथि थप आर्थिक भार पर्ने भएको छ । दूरसञ्चार सेवा दस्तुर टेलिकम्युनिकेसन सर्भिस चार्ज (टीएससी) सम्बन्धी कर दायित्वलाई कारण देखाउँदै मूल्य बढाइएको भनिए पनि त्यसको अनुपात, कानुनी आधार र नियामक निकायको भूमिकामाथि गम्भीर प्रश्न उठेका छन् ।

इन्टरनेट सेवा प्रदायकहरूको संस्था इन्टरनेट सेवा प्रदायक संघ नेपाल (आईस्पान) को अगुवाइमा मूल्यवृद्धिमा कार्टेलिङ भएको आरोप छ । केही प्रदायकले उपभोक्ताले यसअघि तिर्दै आएको शुल्कको तुलनामा दोब्बरसम्म मूल्य बढाउन सक्ने गरी नयाँ दर घोषणा गरेका छन् ।

तर, इन्टरनेटको मूल्यवृद्धि गर्नुअघि कानुनअनुसार नेपाल दूरसञ्चार प्राधिकरणबाट स्वीकृति लिइएको छैन । यस प्रकरणमा नियामक नेपाल दूरसञ्चार प्राधिकरण र सञ्चार तथा सूचना प्रविधि मन्त्रालयको भूमिका पनि प्रश्नको घेरामा परेको छ ।

उपभोक्तालाई प्रत्यक्ष असर पर्ने गरी मूल्य बढाइएको अवस्थामा नियामक निकायले के कदम चाल्यो भन्ने प्रश्न उठेको छ।

नेपाल प्रेस ले दूरसञ्चार सेवाको मूल्य निर्धारणसम्बन्धी कानुनी व्यवस्था, टीएससी विवाद र प्रमुख इन्टरनेट सेवा प्रदायकहरूको विगत सात आर्थिक वर्षको नाफासम्बन्धी विवरणलाई आधार बनाएर यस विषयको अध्ययन गरेको छ ।

नेपाल प्रेसलाई उपलब्ध गराइएको आर्थिक वर्ष २०७५/७६ देखि २०८१/८२ सम्मका केही प्रमुख इन्टरनेट सेवा प्रदायकका वार्षिक लेखापरीक्षण विवरणमा कम्पनीहरू नाफामा सञ्चालन भएको देखिन्छ ।

यसरी मुनाफा कमाउँदै सञ्चालनमा आउँदा समेत TSC को लागि प्रति महिना प्रति ग्राहक अधिकतमा १६ (सोह्र) रूपैयाँदेखि २५ (पच्चिस) रूपैयाँसम्म लागत बढ्ने अवस्थामा एकै पटक प्रति ग्राहक प्रति महिना १००० (एक हजार) रूपैयाँ सम्म थप बढी रकम असुल गर्न खोजिएको देखिन्छ ।

नियामक निकाय प्राधिकरण र सञ्चार मन्त्रालय निरीह भएका हुन् वा तिनै निकायहरूसँगको सेटिङ्गमा ISP हरुले अचाक्ली मूल्यवृद्धि गरेका हुन् ? भन्ने प्रश्न समेत उठेको छ ।

दूरसञ्चार ऐन, २०५३ को दफा ४२ ले दूरसञ्चार सेवाको शुल्क निर्धारणसम्बन्धी व्यवस्था अनुसार सेवाको शुल्क उचित र मनासिब हुनुपर्ने तथा शुल्क लागू गर्नुअघि कम्तीमा तीन महिनाअगावै प्राधिकरणबाट स्वीकृति लिएर सार्वजनिक गर्नुपर्ने व्यवस्था छ।

सेवाको शुल्क निर्धारण गर्दा सेवा प्रदायकको वास्तविक लागतलाई आधार बनाउनुपर्ने विषय पनि महत्त्वपूर्ण हुन्छ। त्यसैले इन्टरनेट सेवा प्रदायकले मूल्य बढाउँदा लागतमा भएको वास्तविक परिवर्तन, कर दायित्व र सेवाको गुणस्तरमा आएको परिवर्तनजस्ता पक्ष स्पष्ट पार्नुपर्ने हुन्छ ।

यदि प्राधिकरणको स्वीकृतिबिना वा कानुनी प्रक्रियाविपरीत मूल्य बढाइएको हो भने त्यो नियामकीय परीक्षणको विषय बन्नेछ । त्यसैगरी, लागतको तुलनामा अस्वाभाविक रूपमा उच्च शुल्क निर्धारण गरिएको हो भने प्राधिकरणको दायित्व हुन्छ यसमा लगाम लगाउने ।

यद्यपि,मूल्यवृद्धि कानुनविपरीत भएको निष्कर्षमा पुग्नुअघि सम्बन्धित प्रदायकले सार्वजनिक गरेका दर, प्राधिकरणको स्वीकृति र लागू भएका निर्णयको आधिकारिक विवरण परीक्षण गर्न आवश्यक छ।

नेपाल सरकारले आर्थिक ऐन, २०७५ देखि दूरसञ्चार सेवामा टीएससी लगाउँदै आएको छ ।सुरुमा १३ प्रतिशत रहेको यस्तो दस्तुर हाल १० प्रतिशत छ ।

फिक्स्ड वायर्ड ब्रोडब्यान्ड सेवामा लाग्ने महसुलको बढीमा ५० प्रतिशतसम्मको मर्मतसम्भार शुल्कमा टीएससी नलाग्ने व्यवस्था आर्थिक ऐनहरूमा गरिएका छ। तर, इन्टरनेट सेवा प्रदायकहरूले ग्राहकको मासिक बिलमा इन्टरनेट सेवा र मर्मतसम्भार सेवाको शुल्क ५०-५० प्रतिशतका दरले छुट्याएर बिलिङ गर्दै आएको विषय विवादमा छ ।

दूरसञ्चार नियमावली, २०५४ को नियम १५ (ज) ले सेवा बिग्रिएमा प्रदायकले निःशुल्क मर्मत गर्नुपर्ने व्यवस्था गरेको छ। २०७६ साउन १५ मा गरिएको नवौँ संशोधनबाट फिक्स्ड वायर्ड ब्रोडब्यान्ड सेवाको महसुलमा बढीमा ५० प्रतिशतसम्म मर्मतसम्भार शुल्क लिन सकिने व्यवस्था थपिएको थियो ।

तर, मर्मतसम्भार शुल्क लिन पाउने व्यवस्था र नियमित मासिक बिलमा स्वतः आधा रकम मर्मतसम्भारका नाममा छुट्याउन पाउने विषय एउटै होइनन्। त्यसैले बिलिङको अभ्यास नियमावली र आर्थिक ऐनको मर्मअनुकूल छ कि छैन भन्ने विषयमा स्पष्ट नियामकीय व्याख्या आवश्यक देखिन्छ।

नेपाल टेलिकमबाहेकका केही इन्टरनेट सेवा प्रदायकले मासिक बिलमा इन्टरनेट र मर्मतसम्भार शुल्क बराबर देखाएर सरकारले प्राप्त गर्नुपर्ने टीएससीको गणना हुने आधार घटाएको विषयमा ठूला करदाता कार्यालयले प्रश्न उठाएको थियो।
